transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-04 14:00 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Mark Davis (Arcadia CTO), Sara Kim (Arcadia Head of ML), Luis Ortega (Arcadia Platform)

Auto-summary:
Alex ran a console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and a token-level cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for a POC; primary concerns are cost predictability, per-route monitoring for retail storefront flows, and PCI/data residency constraints. SE discussed batching, KV/prefix caching, and Optimize recommendations. Agreed next steps: send pricing, SOC2/network docs, schedule benchmarks and POC scope.

Topics:
- Console usage analytics overview
- Per-route dashboards and custom routing labels
- Cost breakdown (token-level, per-route) and cost control levers
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and SLA
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- POC benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run through the Redwood console - focused on the usage analytics and cost breakdown per route, so you can see the economics per feature. Priya and I will demo, and then we'll leave time for Qs.
[00:17] Mark Davis: thanks, Alex. just so you know we have a tight timeline, goal is pilot in april, production summer. cost predictability is big for us.
[00:25] Alex Chen: totally understood. quick ask — Luis, could you share estimated qps and token distribution in chat after? that'll help shape the benchmark.
[00:33] Luis Ortega: yep i'll share after, we have two main routes: 'search-assist' where average prompt is ~120 tokens and 'checkout-bot' ~240 tokens, peak qps around 60.
[00:45] Priya Rao: great, i'll show how route labeling maps to per-route dashboards so you can see latency, error, and token costs per route.
[00:58] Priya Rao: (screen share) here is the usage analytics home - you can filter by model, by route tag, by time window. token breakdown is shown at top, then a per-route table. note that the token cost column factors in the model variant and any quantization profile we choose.
[01:20] Sara Kim: sorry, did you say quantization affects cost column? can you explain briefly?
[01:26] Priya Rao: yeah, so the platform has model variants and quantized builds — for example a 4-bit quantized variant reduces GPU memory and per-token charge because it lets us use more efficient kernels; the console applies the cost-per-token mapping for each variant so the per-route cost reflects that. there can be small quality deltas, we surface evals if available.
[01:45] Mark Davis: okay — our legal/security folks will want to understand KMS and audit logs too, is that in the console?
[01:53] Alex Chen: good point — we have an observability pane that links to audit logs and key rotation events; i'll share SOC2 and network architecture doc after. the console can show per-API-key usage and activity which helps for compliance.
[02:10] Priya Rao: jumping back to the per-route view — you can click into 'checkout-bot' and see token histogram, latency p95, and cost breakdown by model call (e.g., generation vs embeddings if mixed). we also surface suggestions from Redwood Optimize — it will recommend batching window, KV cache TTLs, and a quantization profile based on observed sequence lengths.
[02:34] Mark Davis: can Optimize recommend different models per route? like cheaper model for search and higher quality for checkout?
[02:40] Priya Rao: yes, that's one of the routing policies — you can set per-route model mappings and fallback tiers. the console shows expected cost delta if you switch route X to model Y, including throughput implications.
[02:55] Sara Kim: i remember seeing something about prefix caching — how does that show up?
[03:00] Priya Rao: prefix/KV cache is surfaced in the route detail; we show hit rates and how much token cost you're saving. for chat or repeated prompts caching can reduce tokens by up to 30-60% depending on reuse.
[03:16] Mark Davis: about Dedicated vs Hosted — our compliance team leans to Dedicated with VPC for september, but for pilot we might start hosted. overhead of changing models later?
[03:26] Alex Chen: switching between hosted and dedicated is designed to be smooth — same API and rollouts. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation; pricing is commit-based but offers better unit economics at scale. we can simulate a Dedicated SKU for your traffic in the POC so you can compare.
[03:43] Luis Ortega: any limits on custom kernel/quant builds on Private?
[03:48] Priya Rao: on Private you get more control; we do offer kernel-level tuning in collaboration with our infra team. for VPC deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and on-prem options for air-gapped installs.
[04:05] Alex Chen: circling back - here's the per-token cost waterfall — requests -> model variant -> batching efficiency -> cache hits -> final token charge. the console gives a token-level breakdown so you can attribute spend to routes and to users/API keys.
[04:24] Sara Kim: i see a spike in costs on that day, what's the drill down?
[04:28] Priya Rao: you can drill into time slices — e.g., a campaign caused longer prompts and higher generation lengths. we also surface anomalies and can tie them to routes or API keys.
[04:40] Mark Davis: are there rate-limiting knobs per route? we want to throttle checkout-bot differently than search.
[04:46] Priya Rao: yep, per-route rate limits and quotas are configurable; you can also set cost-based hard limits so a route can't exceed a budget.
[04:56] Alex Chen: one more demo piece — cost forecasting. we show forecasted monthly spend by extrapolating current trends and a "what-if" where you change model or enable caching.
[05:08] Mark Davis: that would be useful for finance sign-off.
[05:12] Priya Rao: absolutely. also for the POC we recommend two tracks: a cost-focused run that sweeps model variants and batching, and a latency SLO run to validate p95 under peak qps.
[05:25] Luis Ortega: how hands-on is Redwood for the POC? we have a small infra team.
[05:29] Alex Chen: our SEs run the benchmark scaffolding and help configure routes, but we keep knowledge transfer in the plan — you'll get runbooks and dashboards.
[05:37] Sara Kim: what about data residency / retention? do you support region-locking?
[05:42] Priya Rao: yes, region routing and retention policies are configurable; for Hosted we have region options and for Dedicated/Private you control the region/cluster entirely. retention windows and log export are configurable and can be auto-archived to your S3.
[05:55] Mark Davis: any mention of competitors — curious how Redwood compares on observability vs others?
[05:59] Alex Chen: compared to vendor X (OpenAI) — we surface per-route economics and more detailed trace-level token breakdown, and compared to Anthropic we offer dedicated reserved pools and more ops controls for enterprises.
[06:15] Priya Rao: quick note on accuracy regressions — the console can tie evals to prompt sets so if you switch quant profiles or models you can see quality regressions and rollback.
[06:27] Mark Davis: nice. ok let's talk logistics for the benchmark.
[06:30] Alex Chen: recommended: share a week's traffic sample and the three priority routes, we'll run a POC bench with your sample, try two model families and quant levels, and return per-route cost/latency report.
[06:42] Luis Ortega: i'll get the traffic dump by friday.
[06:44] Alex Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[06:48] Sara Kim: one quick thing — will the console show cost per-customer or per-storefront? we have multi-tenant shops.
[06:54] Priya Rao: yes, you can tag requests with customer_id and use route tags; the dashboard supports multi-dim breakdowns so you can see cost by tenant.
[07:04] Mark Davis: great.
[07:08] Alex Chen: ok recap of next steps: i'll send pricing and SOC2/network docs; Priya will set up the benchmark; Luis will share traffic; we'll schedule the benchmark the week of march 9.
[07:20] Mark Davis: sounds good, thanks Alex, Priya.
[07:23] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the POC scope doc and a calendar invite.

End of transcript.
